thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: p99 latency breach in eu-west cluster (> 5.0s) for inference-service-prod. Triggered at 2025-06-12T07:20:00Z. Pager: oncall-sre@example.com
PagerDuty: Incident INC-78532 created and assigned to Oncall SRE

Alice: acked. I'm on it. Pulling dashboards now. :eyes:

Ben: saw same on synthetic monitors. p95 is okay but p99 spike across many hosts. Looks correlated with a recent canary deploy to inference-runtime v3.2.1-canary.

Carol: checking autoscaler + GPU allocation. Autoscaler shows a burst of concurrent requests, pods healthy but long tails on token generation. KV cache miss rate spiked ~3x.

Dinesh: adding context: we enabled large-batch batching for small-chat workload at ~07:10 to improve throughput (feature flag). Could be increasing queueing latency for some requests. Rolling that back now.

Alice: good call. Rollback flag first. Dinesh, can you flip ff_chat_large_batches=false?

Dinesh: flipping now.

incident-bot: action: feature-flag toggle request submitted by Dinesh.

Carol: I'm seeing a queued backlog on the sidecar at pod inference-rt-7f6b; continuous batching backlog length increased. Evicting queued batches might help. Trying a graceful drain on that pod to force rebalancing.

Ben: while that happens, consider routing a percentage of traffic to the smaller quantized variant (gptq-small) to reduce tail latency. We can set smart-routing policy to prefer low-latency models for interactive routes.

Alice: agree. Carol, can you spin up a quick routing override to shift 20% of chat traffic to model=gptq-small? Use the console quick-route override.

Carol: applying override: 
```
POST /api/v1/routes/override
{ "route": "chat.completions.prod", "weight": { "gpt-full": 80, "gptq-small": 20 }, "reason": "p99 mitigation" }
```
Response: 202 accepted.

PagerDuty: Acknowledgement recorded by Alice. Escalation policy: if not resolved in 15m will escalate to SRE Lead.

Eva: tagging product/customer-impact: we saw error budget alerts for several customers using low-latency chat endpoints. ETA on mitigation?

Alice: rolling mitigation steps: 1) ff rollback (done by Dinesh) 2) route override to gptq-small (applied by Carol) 3) scale up reserve pool by +4 GPUs (pending) 4) investigate canary shard.

Frank: scaling reserve pool now: `kubectl scale --replicas=4 deployment/reserve-inference-pool -n prod` — started.

Ben: also temp reduce max_batch_size to 8 on runtime for chat route to reduce queueing: 
```
PUT /api/v1/runtime/config
{ "route": "chat.completions.prod", "max_batch_size": 8 }
```
Applied. Expect CPU/GPU efficiency hit but should lower tail.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: Alice set priority to P1 and added escalation target SRE Lead.

Carol: KV cache miss rate still elevated but dropping since ff rollback. Rolling restart completed on inference-rt-7f6b; pod rejoined healthy. Latency tail improving on that host.

Alice: watching metrics: p99 dropped from ~6.2s to ~3.8s after overrides. p95 steady ~420ms. Keeping checks for next 10m.

PagerDuty: Reminder: please add short incident summary and check-in cadence.

Dinesh: quick note: the canary had a minor change to the scheduler that enabled longer batch accumulation for throughput. That interacts poorly with KV-cache miss storms. We'll roll canary back in the next release and add guardrail to prevent enabling batching on low-KV-hit routes.

Eva: customer comms: flagging customers A, B for potential degraded experience. Recommend holding off on proactive emails until we confirm stability (next 30m).

Frank: reserve pool scaled, added 4 GPU nodes, autoscaler response increased available capacity. New pods are healthy.

Ben: I'm running a quick replay of request traces for the top 5 problematic user sessions. Looks like requests hitting large context windows triggered longer generation times; combining with batching gave high tail.

Alice: plan: keep override and reduced batch_size for 30m, monitor p99. If stable, we'll gradually remove overrides and restore batch_size to original. If not stable in 15m escalate to SRE Lead for bridge + postmortem.

Carol: can we add a temporary circuit-breaker to prevent large-batch accumulation when KV miss rate > 2x baseline? I can push a quick patch to runtime config.

Dinesh: implementing circuit-breaker threshold: `kvcache_miss_threshold=2.0` — deploying.

incident-bot: Alice updated PagerDuty: status = acknowledged, mitigation steps in progress. Next check-in in 5m.

Alice: 07:35 check-in: p99 now ~2.1s, tail improving. No escalations yet. Keeping watch.

Eva: documenting customer impact: region eu-west intermittent high-latency affecting chat completions for heavy-context sessions; no data loss, degraded latency only.

Ben: note for postmortem: root cause candidate = canary scheduler change enabling longer batch accumulation + KV cache miss storm. Interaction with autoscaler slow-to-react made tail worse.

Frank: will keep reserve nodes live for another hour to avoid flap.

Alice: handoff: I'm heading out in 25m; Frank will be primary for next hour then hand to night-oncall. If p99 creeps above 3s, please page immediately.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident still open. Next auto-reminder in 10m.

Alice: thanks team. Adding final note to thread and will add a short timeline to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

Frank: confirming — will update ticket and stand by for handoff.

PagerDuty: Incident INC-78532 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: Alice.

Alice: closing slack thread for now — will reopen if we see re-regression.
